text:
sre-bot: ALERT: gpu-pool-eu-west-1 queue depth > 95% for 6m, instant throttles firing

maria_n: seeing a ton of 429s from hosted API, customers complaining latency spikes
ajay_p: looking at metrics — scheduler backlog spiking, pod create latencies rising
kevin_w: can someone check autoscaler events? might be scale-thrash on cluster side
lina_s: logs show admission controller started rejecting requests: "insufficient gpus"
chao: also noticing a slow control-plane due to etcd leader election around same time
maria_n: are we sure it's not a networking partition in eu-west? some pods in AZ-b lost node heartbeats
ajay_p: network flaps yes, EC2 instance detach + kubelet reconnects -> many pods recreated and requeued work
kevin_w: that plus models with large KV caches caused memory pressure when pods landed on remaining nodes
lina_s: when eviction started, the request router retried to other pools -> cascade into us-west capacity which then hit its own limits
ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2024-042, paging oncall-sre
chao: root cause looks like simultaneous AZ node loss + insufficient admission control to gate incoming requests by GPU tokens
maria_n: we had admission control but token bucket config was permissive during peak (burst allowed), so backlog exceeded queue length
ajay_p: and the fallback was configured to route to larger models in other regions without checking remaining capacity -> amplified load
kevin_w: so sequence = AZ node failures -> pod churn -> queue backlog -> permissive admission -> cross-region routing -> cross-zone saturation -> control-plane latency -> leader election -> more churn
lina_s: impact: 22% of requests returned 429s for ~40 minutes, median latency for successful requests up from 110ms -> 1.3s, two high-value customers saw 5xxs during failover
maria_n: mitigation applied: tightened admission token bucket to 50r/s per pool, disabled cross-region fallback for saturated pools, temporarily increased drop-priority for long-running low-priority jobs
kevin_w: also pinned autoscaler cooldown to 3m to avoid thrash, and circuit-breaker now short-circuits to cached responses
chao: applied etcd tuning: reduced election timeout jitter and added health checks to avoid leader flip during transient network issues
ajay_p: long-term: we need capacity-aware routing — don't fall back to regions without checking remaining GPU tokens + better global backpressure signals
lina_s: add a pre-flight gRPC admission handshake that returns estimated queue wait time; callers can choose degraded mode instead of retrying
maria_n: follow-ups: 1) postmortem writeup due EOD today, 2) change admission config canary to test cluster before global rollouts, 3) run chaos test for AZ node loss next week
kevin_w: I'll own capacity-aware routing design, target PR in 2 weeks
ajay_p: I'll add unit and e2e tests for token-bucket behavior and simulate burst cases
chao: ops will schedule etcd stress test and adjust runbook for leader election incidents
ops-bot: actions assigned: kevin_w (route-design), ajay_p (admission-tests), chao (etcd-runbook).
maria_n: thanks all — logging this as a Sev2 postmortem in pager duty and tagging customers impacted for outreach
kevin_w: small note: add per-API-key rate-limits tied to reserved GPU capacity so big customers can't trigger fleet-wide backpressure
lina_s: agree. also recommend we add a dashboard for "effective GPU headroom" per region so SRE can see real-time admission health
chao: last thought — consider proactive rebalancer that avoids moving large KV-cache-heavy models into a shrinking pool during high churn
maria_n: 👍 closing thread, will paste PM when postmortem doc is ready
